content:
Hey, I am not exactly a new member - I have been a member of this Zulip group for some time now. But, I have only properly opened it and asked questions on two occasions (the sheer volume of unread messages scare me). So, I kinda have an organizational question.

  1. How do I find out what projects people are working on? There is a section called "Project announcements", but there seems to be so many unread messages there (because I am rarely here), it's hard to keep track.
  2. If I would like to propose a new project, how do I do it? That is another reason I wanted to check the projects that are being worked on.
  3. If I have Lean related questions, where do I post it? The two times I did, I believe I used this "new members" section, but I think it would be silly to keep using it indefinitely.

For 1) and 2) this has historically happened organically, but there is a new channel/repo #Project intentions you might find helpful.

For 3) it really depends on the question. There is #general, #Is there code for X?, #mathlib4, #metaprogramming / tactics etc. If a moderator notices that a message would be clearly better-suited for another channel, they may move it for you.
If you feel your questions are beginner's questions (which are fine, by the way! everybody starts as a beginner), then using #**new members> is perfectly fine.
@Chris Henson and @Michael Rothgang thanks a lot for both your answers. They are really helpful :)
@Chris Henson it seems like "Project intentions" only has posts by a bot. Should I just post there myself nevertheless, or something else maybe?
No, you should not post there. The messages in that channel are are generated from https://github.com/leanprover-community/project-intentions, which has instructions in the README.

@Chris Henson I put my project up on the "Project Intentions" section as you had mentioned. But, I do not know how to switch it from the "No Status" section to the "In Progress" section. Could you please help me with that?
